_doc: #783 THE ONE DECLARATION of every place a fleet app keeps state, read by (1) libs:core FleetConfig — the export/import contract every fleet app serves through its <package>.fleetconfig provider, which exports/imports exactly the migrating stores declared here and nothing else; #796 this file lives in the SuperApp only (it is fleet-wide data: baked into libs:core it rebuilt all 33 apps on every edit) and TRAVELS WITH EVERY CALL -- FleetConfig.export/import put it in the call extras, each app's provider applies what it is handed; (2) the SuperApp Account (Runtime reads it, Drift diffs it, server→runtime and the new-phone migration apply it); (3) cloud-vault C_A1-configs/emit.py (the `settings` section carries one entry per app below); (4) fleet-config-guard.yml, which fails when the code opens a store this file does not declare. Edit here, never a copy.

classes.config: user-facing setting that defines "my configuration": migrates to a new phone (exported, diffed, applied).
classes.secret: a credential: migrates through the vault, always masked on screen (exported only to fleet-signed callers).
classes.device: never migrates: install ids, device keys, caches, cursors, trackers, sync state, migration markers.
classes.content: user data that lives on a server or in the shared store: only the account link migrates, never the bytes.

kinds.prefs: SharedPreferences — exported and imported by the contract with no app code.
kinds.encrypted: EncryptedSharedPreferences (default MasterKey, AES256_SIV keys / AES256_GCM values) — exported and imported by the contract through the same cipher.
kinds.datastore: Preferences DataStore — declared and counted; the contract cannot write it under the app's live in-memory copy, so it is reported as not yet covered.
kinds.room: Room database — declared and counted; config inside a database is reported as not yet covered.
kinds.file: a file the app keeps (dotfiles, json, models) — declared per app/lib under `items`.

<default>.doc: The app's default SharedPreferences (<package>_preferences): HeliBoard keyboard settings (libs:keyboard), translate settings (libs:translate), the vault's bwPreferencesStorage keys, and the terminals' settings (Termux TermuxAppSharedPreferences: fontsize, log_level, extra keys, soft keyboard, screen-on; the session cursor, notification id and per-boot counters are device). Element X keeps only DI scaffolding here (device). bg_startup_tracing is the WebView's own startup-tracing flag, written into any app that hosts a WebView (device). Device for apps whose current code reads none of it: mail (the FairEmail-era settings the Sterna clone, 8b7ca107d, never reads — migrating them would only plant dead keys), notes (an intro-shown marker only) and office (the asset-extraction commit marker only).

AppCenter.doc: Legacy Xamarin AppCenter prefs read once by LegacyAppCenterMigrator to carry old Bitwarden settings forward; migration source only.

PUSH_NOTIFICATIONS.doc: Mattermost per-notification-group JSON used to dedupe/clear delivered notifications; transient.

VERSION_PREFERENCE.doc: Mattermost app-version marker that resets the notification cache on upgrade.

account_data_migration.doc: #867 whether this app has already copied the imported configs, profile and S/R/L account files over from the Cloud Account app. It records this phone's progress, never configuration.

account_migrate.doc: #783 the new-phone migration journal: per app, the hash of the declared copy applied and its outcome, so a re-run resumes. It describes this phone's progress, never configuration.

acode_auth_secure.doc: Acode account auth token/session held in EncryptedSharedPreferences (Authenticator.PREFS_FILENAME).

acode_sftp_profiles_v1.doc: Acode saved SFTP connection profiles (host/user/credentials) via SftpSecurityStore; credential-bearing so secret.

acode_theme.doc: Acode editor colour scheme (key per theme colour) written by System.java so the crash/launch screens match the chosen theme; a user theme choice.

adb_shell.doc: Per-install random token shared with the local adb shell server; install identity.

ads.doc: Acode RewardPassManager ad-reward pass state; per-install ad counters, not configuration.

advisory_feed.doc: Single 'last' poll timestamp throttling the ntfy advisory feed; sync cursor.

agent-auth.doc: #790 the agent CLIs' credentials in each terminal, keyed by the environment variable each CLI reads (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for claude, OPENROUTER_API_KEY for goose and hermes). Configs ▸ Account imports it from the declared profile (settings › termux|nix-on-droid › agent-auth, derived from ai › tokens by the cockpit's agent_auth map); AgentAuth.java writes it on every start to $HOME/<ab_cloud-terminal-store/store.json::agent_auth.env_file> (0600), which login-init.sh sources into every session.

apps_mesh.doc: #793 the Apps Mesh page's chosen chip filter (`filter`): which members the page shows first. A view preference, so it moves with the phone; the probe cache itself is a cacheDir file and never migrates.

app_tabs.doc: User-arranged launcher app-tab entries (JSON list under 'entries').

auto_update.doc: Auto-update toggles (enabled, require_silent/unmetered) are settings; last_check/remote digest/bytes/unattended_pass are state.

pass_ledger.doc: #894 What the running fleet pass did per package (installed, needs a tap, failed), the summary signature last shown and the last failure reported per package: pass state, never a setting.

badge_customization.doc: Per-badge notification toggles (enabled/persistent/options) the user set in the notification center.

battery_badge.doc: The Battery badge's short-term rate tracker: the reference sample (time, level, charge counter, direction) and the EMA of the charge or drain rate. Hardware-specific telemetry, rebuilt within minutes.

bundle._doc: #873/#874 THE BUNDLE ROUTES: where each Connections value of Cloud Account's vault (the imported configs blob, `section.key` paths) lands in the fleet, as declared stores. Fleet Setup (libs:account SetupPlan) finds every app that declares the store (used_by its module or one of its libs) and applies the key through that app's `<package>.fleetsetup` provider. A target with `pull` names the app Cloud Account reads the value FROM, once, when its vault holds none (AccountMigrate: the stores SuperApp kept). A value the declared copy's `settings` subtree or the Configs section names itself (app > store > file > key) needs no route. Edit here, never a copy in code; fleet-setup-guard checks every route names a declared store, a key it may migrate and a pull app that declares the store.

_doc_items: apps[].items / libs[].items: configuration kept OUTSIDE a declared store (files, a fork's own database). `store` names the declared store that actually holds it (the contract moves it when that store is portable); `via: install` = reproduced by installing the same build (baked from git); `via: connect` = re-fetched from the vault on Connect. Anything else with a migrating class is a named gap in the coverage.
